Train Test split
```{python, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import sklearn
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.feature_selection import SequentialFeatureSelector
from sklearn.linear_model import PoissonRegressor

# convert R list into dataframe
tornadoes_df = pd.DataFrame(r.tornado_dataset)
x = tornadoes_df.drop(columns=["Monthly_Tornado_Count"]).values
y = tornadoes_df["Monthly_Tornado_Count"].values

# train test split 70 / 30 - СONSTRUCTING AN EFFICIENT MACHINE LEARNING MODEL FOR TORNADO PREDICTION
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    x, y,
    test_size=0.3,
    random_state=42
)

# add first row (column names) to features list
feature_names = tornadoes_df.drop(columns=["Monthly_Tornado_Count"]).columns.tolist()

# Backwards selection using SequentialFeatureSelector
poisson = PoissonRegressor()

# sfs initialization
sfs = SequentialFeatureSelector(
    poisson,
    n_features_to_select = "auto",
    direction="backward", # backward selection - start with all predictors in model
    scoring="r2",
    cv=5,
    n_jobs=1
)

# fit training data only to sfs - prevents leakage
sfs.fit(X_train, y_train) # add feature names back to dataset


selected_mask = sfs.get_support() # int index of features
selected_features = [f for f, s in zip(feature_names, selected_mask) if s] # set names to selected features
selected_idx = [i for i, s in enumerate(selected_mask) if s] # all selected features

# use selected features in training data only
X_train_selected = X_train[:, selected_idx]
X_test_selected = X_test[:, selected_idx]

# unscaled data for r: poisson regression - coefficients automatically scale
r_X_train = X_train_selected 
r_y_train = y_train
r_X_test = X_test_selected
r_y_test = y_test

# scaled data for python
scaler_X = StandardScaler()
scaler_y = StandardScaler()

X_train = scaler_X.fit_transform(X_train_selected) # V1 V2 V3 V4 V5 V6 V7
X_test = scaler_X.transform(X_test_selected)

y_train = scaler_y.fit_transform(y_train.reshape(-1, 1)).ravel()
y_test = scaler_y.transform(y_test.reshape(-1, 1)).ravel()
```

Backwards Selection - Starts with all variables and eliminates least statistically significant
```{python}
print("Selected features:", selected_features)
print("Removed features:", [f for f, s in zip(feature_names,selected_mask) if not s])
```

Do so after train/test split but do only on training data to prevent leakage

R: Poisson Regression
```{r}
# pull variables from python and create dataframe
train_set <- as.data.frame(py$r_X_train)
test_set <- as.data.frame(py$r_X_test)
colnames(train_set) <- py$selected_features
colnames(test_set) <- py$selected_features
train_set$Monthly_Tornado_Count <- as.integer(py$r_y_train)
test_set$Monthly_Tornado_Count <- as.integer(py$r_y_test)

# poisson glm initialization
poisson_model <- glm(Monthly_Tornado_Count ~ ., family = "poisson", data = train_set)

# model summary
summary(poisson_model)

# make predictions using test set
y_pred <- predict(poisson_model, newdata = test_set, type = "response")

mae <- mean(abs(test_set$Monthly_Tornado_Count - y_pred))
mse <- mean((test_set$Monthly_Tornado_Count - y_pred)^2)

plot(poisson_model)

poisson_aic <- AIC(poisson_model)
print(mae)
print(mse)
print(poisson_aic)
```

Python: Random Forest Regressor
```{python}
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.datasets import make_regression
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, r2_score

# random forest regressor initialization
rfr_regressor = RandomForestRegressor(
    n_estimators=200, # how to choose n_estimators
    random_state=42,
    oob_score=True # outputs model fit score
)

# fit to training today
rfr_regressor.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("Out-of-Bag Score:", rfr_regressor.oob_score_)

# predictions
y_pred = rfr_regressor.predict(X_test)

mse = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred)
r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_pred)

print("Mean Squared Error:", mse)
print("R-squared:", r2)
print()
```

SVM
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.svm import SVR

# LINEAR: svm initialization
svr_linear = SVR(kernel='linear', C=100, epsilon=0.1)
# fit to training data
svr_linear.fit(X_train, y_train)
# predictions - linear fit
y_pred_linear = svr_linear.predict(X_test)

# POLY: svm initialization
svr_poly = SVR(kernel='poly', C=100, epsilon=0.1)
# fit to training data
svr_poly.fit(X_train, y_train)
# predictions - linear fit
y_pred_poly = svr_poly.predict(X_test)

# RBF (Radial Basis Function): svm initialization
svr_rbf = SVR(kernel='rbf', C=100, gamma=0.5, epsilon=0.1)
# fit to training data 
svr_rbf.fit(X_train, y_train)
# predictions - rbf fit
y_pred_rbf = svr_rbf.predict(X_test)

sorted_idx = np.argsort(X_test[:, 0])

X_test_sorted = X_test[sorted_idx]
y_test_sorted = y_test[sorted_idx]

y_pred_linear_sorted = y_pred_linear[sorted_idx]
y_pred_poly_sorted = y_pred_poly[sorted_idx]
y_pred_rbf_sorted = y_pred_rbf[sorted_idx]
```

Linear SVM Visualization
```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(5, 5))
plt.scatter(y_test, y_pred_linear, color='green', alpha=0.5, label='Actual vs Predicted')
plt.plot([y_test.min(), y_test.max()],
         [y_test.min(), y_test.max()],
         color='black', linewidth=2, label='Perfect Fit')

plt.title("Linear Kernel SVR")
plt.xlabel("Predicted Tornado Count (scaled)")
plt.ylabel("Actual Tornado Count (scaled)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

rmse_linear = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_linear))
mse_linear = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_linear)
r2_linear = r2_score(y_test, y_pred_linear)

print("Linear SVR R^2:", r2_linear)
print("Linear SVR RMSE:", rmse_linear)
print("Linear SVR MSE:", mse_linear)
```

Implementation of Zero-Inflated Poisson
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(pscl)
library(boot)
```

```{r}
zip_model <- zeroinfl(Monthly_Tornado_Count ~ ., data = train_set)
summary(zip_model)

zip_null <- zeroinfl(Monthly_Tornado_Count ~ 1, data = train_set)
1 - as.numeric(logLik(zip_model)) / as.numeric(logLik(zip_null))

zip_aic <- AIC(zip_model)
print(zip_aic)
```

```{r}
zinb_model <- zeroinfl(Monthly_Tornado_Count ~ ., data = train_set, dist="negbin")
summary(zinb_model)

zip_null <- zeroinfl(Monthly_Tornado_Count ~ 1, data = train_set)
1 - as.numeric(logLik(zip_model)) / as.numeric(logLik(zip_null))

zinb_aic <- AIC(zinb_model)
print(zinb_aic)
```
